title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Ops Procedures, Top Support Issues
author: Sophia Li
content:
Purpose

This document defines the canonical structure and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference focused on: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. The goal is to make docs consistent, discoverable, and fast to update so engineers and customers can ship production integrations reliably.

Scope and audience

- Scope: All public and internal SDK guides (Python, TypeScript, Go), quickstarts and starter templates, canonical API examples, and the operational workflow for publishing and triaging DevEx docs.
- Audience: Developer experience engineers, SDK maintainers, docs writers, solutions engineers, customer success engineers, and on-call support.

Owner and escalation

- Primary owner: DevEx (eng-developer-experience).
- Secondary owners: SDK maintainers (runtime-services), Solutions Engineering for customer-specific templates.
- Escalation path: author -> DevEx lead -> Head of Developer Experience -> Eng SRE (for infra-related docs).

High-level principles

1. Single source of truth: every SDK or quickstart must map to one canonical Confluence page and link to code in the SDK repo.
2. Reproducible examples: all examples must be runnable end-to-end in a local environment or the provided sandbox and include explicit dependency pins.
3. Minimal friction: quickstarts should get a developer from zero to a simple request in under 10 minutes.
4. Observability-first: examples should include telemetry snippets (metrics/logging) and links to console dashboards where applicable.

Recommended doc structure (applies to SDK guides and quickstarts)

- Title: short, descriptive.
- Short intro (1-2 paragraphs) with use case and target audience.
- Prerequisites: OS, runtime, SDK version, API key scope.
- Quickstart (copy-paste runnable), then deeper examples.
- Common pitfalls & troubleshooting.
- Related templates and links.
- Changelog and maintenance notes.

Example header template (copy into new pages)

- Title: <one-line summary>
- Summary: 1-2 sentence elevator pitch
- Audience: e.g. "Product engineers building in-app chat"
- Maintainers: team and primary contacts
- SDK versions: list (e.g. Python >=1.4.0, TS >=0.9.2)

SDK Guides: conventions and requirements

- Language support: Python, TypeScript/Node, Go (priority). Other SDKs added by demand.
- Versioning: Include the SDK semver badge at top and a compatibility table linking to the Redwood API surface and runtime versions.
- Code style: examples use the official SDKs and are formatted with black/eslint/gofmt.
- Dependency pins: include exact pip/npm/go module versions in the Quickstart.
- Test harness: every guide must include a short unit/integration test or a link to the example repo test.

Mandatory checklist for SDK guide PRs

1. Page created in "quickstarts-and-templates" or "docs-site" space as appropriate.
2. Quickstart runs locally using the pinned dependencies.
3. CI includes a smoke test that executes the example in a container.
4. Reviewer from SDK team signs off.
5. Add labels: language, sdk, quickstart, example.

Quickstarts & templates: canonical starter kits

DevEx maintains a set of starter templates intended for fast onboarding. Each template is a small repo (or mono-repo folder) with: Dockerfile, README, pinned deps, env example, and a sample app that makes calls to Redwood API. Available templates:

- web-chat-react-template (React + Redwood JS SDK)
- serverless-function-starter (AWS Lambda + Node SDK)
- backend-batch-embeddings (Python + Celery)
- rust-embedder (community-maintained, experimental)

How to publish a new template

1. Create repo or folder under git repo: devex-templates/<name>.
2. Add README, LICENSE, Dockerfile, and example app.
3. Add a Confluence page under quickstarts-and-templates linking to the repo + usage instructions.
4. Run template smoke test in CI and add a GitHub action that populates the Confluence preview (optional).

Template metadata table (display on Confluence)

| Template | Language | Purpose | Maintainer | Last validated |
| web-chat-react-template | TypeScript | In-app chat with streaming | devex-ui | 2026-01-05 |
| serverless-function-starter | Node | Short-lived inference calls | serverless-team | 2026-01-20 |
| backend-batch-embeddings | Python | High-volume embedding jobs | infra-ml | 2025-12-12 |

API examples: canonical patterns

Provide short, idiomatic examples for the most common patterns. Each example must include: expected inputs, example request, expected response, and common errors. Include both HTTP/REST and SDK variants. Examples to maintain:

- Simple generation (sync)
- Streaming generation (client-side streaming + reconnect)
- Function/tool calling pattern with structured outputs
- Embeddings (batching best-practices)
- Reranking request flow
- Error handling & retries (idempotency keys)

Sample API example (Python, sync generation)

# Install
# pip install redwood-sdk==1.4.0

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1b", prompt="Write an onboarding email for a new user")
print(resp.text)

Docs site operating procedures (publish workflow)

1. Create draft page: author creates a page in Confluence under quickstarts-and-templates.
2. Add metadata: title, space, author, owner_team, reviewers, labels, related_pages.
3. PR process: author opens a docs PR in the documentation repo (if relevant) that references the Confluence page ID.
4. Reviewer checklist: code example validated, runnable, and has a smoke test.
5. Sign-off: at least one SDK maintainer + one DevEx reviewer.
6. Publish and tweet: set status to published, add label "published", and post an internal announcement in #devex-updates.
7. Post-publish verification: run the smoke test in the published environment and add verification log to the page.

Operational runbook for urgent doc fixes

- Trigger: customer-reported incorrect example, security-critical wording, or broken CI.
- Steps:
  1. Author/owner triages and marks page status = draft.
  2. Create emergency PR with fix and include test.
  3. Notify #devex-updates and support leads.
  4. After merge, update Confluence status and add a one-line summary in the change log.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (2025-2026)

1) Symptom: Streaming responses fail intermittently in browser clients.
   - Root cause: client uses long-polling example instead of SSE/websocket; CORS preflight missing for streaming endpoints.
   - Canonical fix: Use the "client-streaming" example in web-chat-react-template. Ensure CORS header "Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET,POST,OPTIONS" and preflight cache. Add sample nginx config to template.

2) Symptom: High per-token cost for embeddings jobs.
   - Root cause: single-item requests instead of batched requests; no quantization-aware model selected.
   - Canonical fix: use batch_embeddings helper in SDK (examples in backend-batch-embeddings) and switch to recommended embedding model: redwood-emb-large-quant (if acceptable for quality).

3) Symptom: Function calling responses return malformed JSON.
   - Root cause: model hallucination around schema boundaries and missing response validation.
   - Canonical fix: add strict output schema validation using Pydantic/TypeScript zod and include defensive parsing in examples.

4) Symptom: Serverless cold-start timeouts on first request.
   - Root cause: un-pinned SDK versions that invoke SDK initialization synchronously in handler.
   - Canonical fix: initialize client outside handler and use lightweight request path in handler; pin SDK to 0.9.x with known cold-start behavior mitigations.

5) Symptom: 401 errors in customer sandbox.
   - Root cause: API key scope mismatch (embedding-only key used for generation).
   - Canonical fix: update quickstart prerequisites and provide an API key scope-check script (examples/api_key_check.sh).

6) Symptom: Rate-limited errors for bursty UI traffic.
   - Root cause: no client-side debounce/throttle and no server-side queueing.
   - Canonical fix: implement client debounce (200-500ms) and server-side token bucket with retry-after handling; add example middleware in serverless template.

7) Symptom: Unexpectedly different outputs between local and hosted.
   - Root cause: model version mismatch (local pinned model differs from hosted default).
   - Canonical fix: include model_version tag in example requests and document model pinning in SDK guide.

8) Symptom: Embedding similarity drift over time.
   - Root cause: model updates without reindexing.
   - Canonical fix: add reindexing playbook to template and recommend nightly incremental reindex with snapshot validation.

9) Symptom: Examples leaking PII in logs.
   - Root cause: example log statements printing full user prompts.
   - Canonical fix: redact or mask PII in logging examples; include a logging policy snippet.

10) Symptom: CI examples sporadically fail due to environment rate limits.
    - Root cause: shared sandbox tokens and no rate-limiting in tests.
    - Canonical fix: add local mocking option (record/replay) for tests and flag CI runs to use a dedicated rate-limited token with reduced concurrency.

Canonical-fix format (for each issue)

- Title: short description
- Symptom: observed behavior
- Root cause: technical explanation
- Fix summary: one-line change to make
- Implementation steps: numbered, with code/commands where applicable
- Validation: how to confirm the fix works (smoke tests, logs, metrics)

Maintenance and review cadence

- Quarterly review: DevEx squad reviews top issues and templates every quarter and updates the canonical fixes list.
- Rolling validation: templates must be revalidated in CI at least once every 90 days.

Metrics and SLOs for docs (operational)

- Page-quality SLO: 95% of published quickstarts must pass the smoke test within 7 days of publishing.
- Time-to-fix SLO for critical doc bugs: 48 hours from report to merged fix.
- Support reduction target: reduce repeat-incidents tied to doc issues by 30% year-over-year.

Appendix: useful commands and snippets

- Check API key scope (bash):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/auth/scope

- Run local quickstart (docker):
  docker build -t web-chat . && docker run -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=${REDWOOD_API_KEY} -p 3000:3000 web-chat

- Run smoke test (pytest):
  pytest tests/smoke/test_quickstart.py -q

Contact and feedback

For doc errors, template requests, or to suggest new examples, open an issue in the devex-docs repo and tag @devex. For customer-facing emergency doc fixes, notify #devex-updates and #support immediately.
